sources: Pinned by sha256 in legallens/ingestion/sources.py (EVERYDAY_PDFS); the PDFs are gitignored in backend/data/raw/everyday/. Act list agreed with the user for ticket 09: Consumer Protection Act 2019, Transfer of Property Act 1882 (Chapter V, leases, only), the four Labour Codes, and (added afterwards, for rental deposits) the Model Tenancy Act 2021. The Indian Contract Act 1872 was added for the Contract explainer (contract-explainer ticket 03), so Flagged clauses have s.27 and s.74 to cite.
verified_against: scripts/verify_everyday_acts.py: published section and chapter totals; the Code on Social Security's section numbers against the 'Arrangement of Sections' of the India Code copy as on 21 November 2025; leftover page furniture, footnotes and amendment marks. NOT verified against India Code's own text for the CPA, the Wages, IR and OSH Codes or the Transfer of Property Act: indiacode.nic.in answered those downloads with 504s (tried 16 November 2026). The Indian Contract Act (192 sections) is checked against its published numbering (1-75 with 19A, 124-238 with 178A; Chapters VII and XI are repealed) and the print's own contents list; its text was not diffed against India Code or the Department's own file (the PDF is a Drishti Judiciary mirror of the Legislative Department print; India Code 504s). The Model Tenancy Act is checked only for 47 clauses in 8 chapters, numbered 1..47 without a gap, and for each clause's side-heading being removed (the table of contents lists the titles); it is not on India Code.
notes: Consumer Protection Act, Code on Wages, Industrial Relations Code, Code on Social Security and OSH Code are the Gazette of India Extraordinary prints as enacted (Acts 35 of 2019, 29 of 2019, 35, 36 and 37 of 2020), so they carry no later amendments. They share the BNS Gazette adapter (gazette_sections); a Chunk is the section's operative text without its marginal title, as for the BNS.

The Gazette prints differ from the BNS's in a few ways the adapter now handles: the 'SEC. 1] THE GAZETTE ...' running head on odd pages, the assent block before the Hindi-font cover on page 1, and an Act-citation note run onto the last line ('enactments.10 of 1897.'). The BNS output is unchanged by these fixes.
The Consumer Protection Act's last section ends 'with regard to the effect of repeal.'; the adapter keeps that short last line.

Status: the six Acts other than the Model Tenancy Act are in_force; the Model Tenancy Act is model. The four Labour Codes were brought into force on 21 November 2025 (per the India Code enforcement date and press reports; not checked against the Gazette notification itself). The Acts they replaced (for example the Minimum Wages Act 1948) are not in the Corpus, so no repealed-to-superseding mapping is recorded.
Square brackets in the Gazette prints are part of the enacted text (for example '[other than those specified in sub-clause (ii)]' in OSH Code section 2) and are kept.

The Transfer of Property Act text is the International Insolvency Institute's print: unofficial, and it keeps amendment footnotes, which the adapter drops, along with sub-headings, '1[' markers and '[***]' deletions. Section 114A is the inserted section (14 Chunks: 105-117 and 114A). The source's own typos are kept (for example 'A.C's lease' in the section 116 illustration).

Model Tenancy Act 2021: the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs text, from a LiveLaw print (unofficial copy). It is a template that States may adopt, not law in force by itself: its own text reads '(Name of State/Union territory) Tenancy Act'. Its Chunks carry the `model` Status (not in force by itself) under the Act name 'Model Tenancy Act'; the LLM prompt and the page say so. The print interleaves each clause's side-heading and Act citations ('41 of' / '2006.') into the text, so the adapter (model_tenancy_sections) removes them by matching the table of contents' titles; a title wrapped across lines or placed in a neighbouring clause's text is removed too, and a short last line that merely repeats a title after an unfinished sentence is kept.
